speak: Chapter one. An electric telescope.
sub: Chapter one. An electric telescope.

sub: A student in Berlin, Paul Nipkow, imagined a disk with holes in a spiral. As it spun, each hole scanned a strip of the image.

speak: He patented it as an electric telescope. He never built it.
sub: He patented it as an electric telescope. He never built it.

speak: A whole photo cannot fit inside a wire at once. But you can slice it into strips.
sub: A whole photo cannot fit inside a wire at once. But you can slice it into strips.

speak: You read each strip from left to right, like a line in a book: light, dark, light. And you send those changes of light as electricity.
sub: You read each strip from left to right, like a line in a book: light, dark, light. And you send those changes of light as electricity.

speak: The idea was there. It would take forty years to see it work.

speak: Chapter two. The dummy's head.
sub: Chapter two. The dummy's head.

speak: In a London attic, a Scotsman named John Logie Baird tried to build it. He put together a machine with spinning disks, motors, and lamps.

speak: When he finally saw the dummy's face on his screen, he ran downstairs.

speak: Chapter three. The furrows.

speak: Chapter four. The dollar sign.
